questions.question_text:
A mobile dog grooming service charges according to the model $C = 25t + 40$, where $C$ is the total charge in dollars and $t$ is the grooming duration in hours.
What does the value $25$ represent?

options.text: The hourly rate of $\$25$ for grooming.
The initial booking fee of $\$25$.
options.why: Confuses the gradient (hourly rate) with the vertical intercept (fixed fee).

options.text: The total cost of $\$25$ for a grooming session.
options.why: Treats the rate per hour as the overall cost regardless of time.

options.text: The number of hours spent grooming the dog.
options.why: Confuses the coefficient $25$ with the independent variable $t$.

questions.solution_text:
The value $25$ is the gradient ($m$).
It represents the hourly rate of $\$25$ for grooming.

questions.question_text:
A commercial print shop calculates the cost of printing $n$ event flyers using $C = 0.08n + 350$, where $C$ is the total cost in dollars.
What does the value $350$ represent?

options.text: The fixed setup cost of $\$350$ before any flyers are printed.
The cost of printing each flyer.
options.why: Confuses the vertical intercept with the gradient (the per-flyer printing cost of $\$0.08$).

options.text: The total number of flyers printed.
options.why: Confuses the constant term with the independent variable $n$.

options.text: The total cost of printing $350$ flyers.
options.why: Interprets the constant $350$ as a number of flyers rather than a dollar amount.

questions.solution_text:
When $n = 0$, $C = 350$.
It represents the fixed setup cost of $\$350$ before any flyers are printed.

questions.question_text:
The total fuel consumed $F$ (in litres) by a diesel generator running between $t = 2$ hours and $t = 10$ hours is modelled by $F = 2.4t + 5$.
Using interpolation, what is the estimated fuel consumed after $6.5$ hours of operation?

options.why: Multiplies $2.4 \times 6.5 = 15.6$ but forgets to add the constant $5$.
Calculates $2.4(6.5 + 5) = 27.6$, incorrectly adding the constant before multiplying.
Rounds $6.5$ to $7$ and computes $2.4(7) + 5 = 21.8 \approx 22$ instead of evaluating at $6.5$.

questions.solution_text:
$F = 2.4(6.5) + 5$
$= 15.6 + 5$
$= 20.6$
The estimated fuel consumed is $20.6$ L.

questions.question_text:
The height $H$ (in centimetres) of a tomato seedling recorded weekly over its first $5$ weeks ($w = 1$ to $w = 5$) is modelled by $H = 4.2w + 10$.
Using extrapolation, what is the predicted height at $w = 8$ weeks?

options.why: Calculates $4.2 \times 8 = 33.6$ but forgets to add the initial height of $10$ cm.
Calculates $4.2(10) + 10 = 52.0$, substituting the constant $10$ instead of the week $8$.
Evaluates at $w = 5$ ($4.2 \times 5 + 10 = 31.0$) rather than extrapolating to $w = 8$.

questions.question_text:
A drone battery discharges during flight according to $B = 100 - 4.5m$, where $B$ is the remaining battery percentage and $m$ is the flight time in minutes.
Why does this model fail for a flight time of $m = 25$ minutes?

options.text: It calculates a negative battery percentage ($-12.5\%$), which is physically impossible.
The flight time of $25$ minutes is too short for the linear model to apply.
options.why: The model is valid for early times; it fails because the battery runs out before $25$ minutes.

options.text: The battery percentage increases beyond $100\%$ after $25$ minutes.
options.why: The gradient is negative, so the percentage decreases into negative values, not above $100\%$.

options.text: The model predicts the drone can fly for up to $100$ minutes before the battery runs out.
options.why: Confuses the vertical intercept ($100\%$ initial charge) with the horizontal intercept ($100$ minutes); the battery depletes when $B = 0$ at $m = 100 \div 4.5 \approx 22.2$ minutes.

questions.solution_text:
$B = 100 - 4.5(25)$
$= 100 - 112.5$
$= -12.5$
A battery level of $-12.5\%$ is impossible; the model fails because the battery is completely depleted at $m \approx 22.2$ minutes.

questions.question_text:
A runner's heart rate $R$ (in beats per minute) during a fitness test at running speeds $v$ between $6$ km/h and $14$ km/h is modelled by $R = 8.5v + 65$.
If this model is used at $v = 28$ km/h, what is the predicted heart rate and why may the prediction be unreliable?

options.text: $303$ bpm; the heart rate may not continue increasing by $8.5$ bpm for each additional km/h.
$238$ bpm; the runner cannot run at a speed of $28$ km/h.
options.why: Computes $8.5 \times 28 = 238$ without adding the starting heart rate of $65$ bpm, and assumes the runner's maximum speed without supporting information.

options.text: $303$ bpm; linear models can never be used to make predictions.
options.why: Incorrectly rejects all linear predictions; a prediction can be reliable when the model fits the observations and remains applicable.

options.text: $273$ bpm; the calculation used the wrong constant term.
options.why: Uses $35$ instead of $65$ for the constant term, giving $8.5(28) + 35 = 238 + 35 = 273$.

questions.solution_text:
$R = 8.5(28) + 65$
$= 238 + 65$
$= 303$
The predicted heart rate is $303$ bpm. The model assumes a constant increase of $8.5$ bpm for each additional km/h. If this rate changes at higher speeds, the prediction will be unreliable; the measurements alone do not establish that the rate continues.

questions.question_text:
A hot bowl of soup cools in a room where the ambient temperature is $20^{\circ}\text{C}$.
For the first $10$ minutes, its temperature $T$ (in $^{\circ}$C) is modelled by $T = 85 - 3.5t$.
Why does this linear model break down if used to predict the temperature at $t = 30$ minutes?

options.text: It predicts $-20^{\circ}\text{C}$, but cooling in this room slows as the soup approaches $20^{\circ}\text{C}$ and does not take it below room temperature.
The soup will freeze into solid ice after $30$ minutes at room temperature.
options.why: Takes the calculated $-20^{\circ}\text{C}$ literally instead of recognising that cooling in a room at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$ does not take the soup below room temperature.

options.text: The initial temperature of $85^{\circ}\text{C}$ was too low for a linear cooling model.
options.why: Incorrectly blames the starting temperature; the limitation is that cooling slows as the soup approaches room temperature.

options.text: The rate of cooling increases over time rather than remaining constant.
options.why: Reverses the change in cooling rate: the soup cools more slowly as it approaches room temperature.

questions.solution_text:
$T = 85 - 3.5(30)$
$= 85 - 105$
$= -20$
The model predicts $-20^{\circ}\text{C}$; cooling in this room cannot take the soup below $20^{\circ}\text{C}$. Cooling slows as the soup approaches room temperature, so the constant decrease of $3.5^{\circ}\text{C}$ per minute no longer applies.
